subject.title: fix(gateway): rate-limit control-plane writes per method with a 30/min budget

question: Should authorized clients receive 30 writes per minute for every control-plane method, or must the gateway retain a client-wide aggregate ceiling alongside method isolation?
rationale: Method isolation is supported by the reported usability problem, but the tenfold per-method increase materially changes the original availability and abuse-protection boundary and requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Add an aggregate ceiling
options.body: Keep method-specific buckets for usability while consuming a second client-wide budget that bounds total control-plane churn.

options.title: Accept 30 per method
options.body: Explicitly adopt the broader authorized-client trust model and provide live evidence that realistic runaway behavior remains acceptably bounded.

options.title: Calibrate a lower budget
options.body: Measure normal Control UI request bursts and choose a smaller per-method allowance without adding a second counter.

recommendation.title: Add an aggregate ceiling
recommendation.body: Keep method-specific buckets for usability while consuming a second client-wide budget that bounds total control-plane churn.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior limiter introduction and security-hardening commits make this the best available owner for the intended protection boundary.
